**Filing gate ①** — user-visible text at a public surface that contradicts a recorded ruling, with a named landing point. **`reach:`** the notification an approver receives when a pending decision is reminded or breaches its SLA reads "A decision on `showcase_expense/EXP_123` is still waiting on you." / "… is overdue." — the object's API name and the record id joined by a slash. The sibling `approval.requested` notification for the same request reads "A decision on Expense Report EXP_123 …", the form ruling B of #23556 / #23594 set for every approval notification body. (Exact wording above is from the code; the object and id are illustrative.)

- `:6534-6550` (`topic: 'approval.sla_breached'`): ``body: `A decision on ${raw.object_name}/${raw.record_id} is overdue.` ``
- `:6923-6927`, `nameSubjectRecord` — the ruled helper: `${this.objectLabelOf(object) ?? object} ${recordId}`, its docblock "[#23594 / #23556 ruling B] … this body is written once at send time, with no per-recipient reader to narrow for, so it stays label-and-id", and "⛔ No title, from any source".
- `:3643` (the `approval.requested` site) says it uses "the same payload shape as `approval.reminder` and every other sibling" — the shape is shared, the subject naming is not.

## Done when

- Both reminder sites and the SLA-breach site name the record through `nameSubjectRecord`, so every approval notification body uses the one ruled form (no title, label and id).
- A pin asserts the reminder and SLA-breach bodies carry the object label, and fails against today's `object_name/record_id`.
